A scientist at heart, much of Pathak's academic work was focused on physics and research related to the solar corona. As a student at the University of Memphis and a recent immigrant to the USA, Sankaet Pathak needed to open a bank account. He was surprised to learn that wasn’t an easy task. Sankaet knew he had to develop a better option not only for himself but for the over 20% of adults in the USA with poor or limited credit history. Sankaet founded Synapse with an eye toward offering a viable alternative to legacy banking systems, while providing operational simplicity, efficiency & ease of integration to perform virtually any banking interaction. Sankaet is launching an AI startup soon called Foundation. Foundation is developing the future of general purpose robotics with the goal to address the labor shortage. Max Faldin, CEO/Founder Silverbird
Max has decades of experience building global IT & fintech businesses. After getting his MBA at Stanford, he co-founded Russia's largest eCommerce company, Wikimart (dubbed "the Amazon of Russia" by Silicon Valley VCs) and raised $50M+ from Tiger Global. He then switched over to work with e-commerce companies in Asia, focusing mainly on payments as a CEO, investor, and advisor to numerous startups. He started Silverbird amidst the pandemic in London, in 2020, after noticing a major banking gap in international trade: millions of underserved SMEs around Africa, Middle East, and Asian regions and beyond were exposed to high fees, unfair rejections, unnecessary paperwork, and outdated regulations. The key pain point was high-value cross-border transactions - something international trade is all about. Silverbird makes cross-border banking business-friendly and international payments borderless, limitless, frictionless and affordable. It can onboard companies traditional banks can't through the use of AI and data-driven KYC which analyzes publicly open customs and supply chain data to assess the risk-profile of a particular SME.

About Sheel Mohnot
Sheel Mohnot built a distinctive fintech investing profile through two successful exits (FeeFighters to Groupon and Innovative Auctions) plus founding Thistle, giving him unusually deep operating experience that he channels into pre-seed and seed investing at Better Tomorrow Ventures. He's known for his "everything is fintech" thesis, obsession with founder speed and tenacity over specific ideas, and building a large social media following that directly generates deal flow—plus he bootstrapped his first fund by funding early deals from his own bank account before raising institutional capital.
Where they've Worked
This is some text inside of a div block.
Sheel Mohnot's Interests
What they've been talking about across their social media accounts
Tracks late-stage private market valuations and fund performance metrics closely, often analyzing specific returns from firms like Benchmark or comparing cost basis to current trading prices for companies such as Databricks and Ramp.
Focuses heavily on the business mechanics of artificial intelligence rather than just the technology, frequently commenting on revenue growth at major labs like Anthropic or drawing parallels between current skepticism of AI profitability and early doubts about Facebook.
Analyzes fintech mergers and acquisitions with a critical eye for strategic logic, such as questioning the synergy between Southeast Asian superapp Grab and US investing platform Stash, or noting the distribution genius behind Mr Beast acquiring the teen banking app Step.
Shares a strong enthusiasm for food trends and culinary discoveries, ranging from the specific delight of discovering flaky salt on desserts at Square's cafeteria to humorous observations about an Indian restaurant chain named after New York burritos.
Appreciates clever marketing arbitrages and unique business hacks, highlighted by his admiration for an Indian e-commerce giant sponsoring the Namibian cricket team to get cheaper visibility during the World Cup.
Interest in unique real estate and cultural artifacts, evidenced by his personal attempt to bid on the house from the show Breaking Bad and his curiosity regarding how ultra-wealthy families allocate their spending.

context.quote: Before fintech was even a common word, Sheel Mohnot saw an opportunity to be a part of the digital transformation of finance and technology.
context.claim: The episode description reports that Mohnot entered fintech early in the sector's development.

context.quote: Mohnot, the co-founder of Better Tomorrow Ventures, talks about his first foray into the fintech world with a non-profit and why he’s dedicated his career to making the consumer experience better.
context.claim: The episode description identifies Mohnot as a Better Tomorrow Ventures co-founder and characterizes his career as focused on improving the consumer experience in fintech.

context.quote: Meet Sheel Mohnot, co-founder and GP at Better Tomorrow Ventures.
context.claim: The episode description identifies Mohnot as a co-founder and general partner at Better Tomorrow Ventures.

context.quote: He started investing out of his own pocket before raising a proof-of-concept fund in 2017, then launched BTV and is now on their third fund.
context.claim: The episode description reports that Mohnot began with personal investing, raised a proof-of-concept fund in 2017, and subsequently launched BTV, which is now on its third fund.

context.quote: Born and raised in Pittsburgh, before entering venture, Sheel lived on $1 a day in India doing microfinance work, built and sold two companies, and co-founded Thistle, a healthy food delivery business now generating north of $100M in revenue.
context.claim: The episode description reports Mohnot's Pittsburgh background, microfinance work in India, two company sales, and role as a Thistle co-founder.

context.quote: Sheel Mohnot is a Co-Founder and General Partner @ Better Tomorrow Ventures, a $225M fund that leads rounds in pre-seed and seed-stage fintech companies globally.
context.claim: The 2022 profile identifies Mohnot as a Better Tomorrow Ventures co-founder and general partner and describes BTV as a $225 million global fintech fund leading pre-seed and seed rounds.

context.quote: Sheel and Jake (his co-founder) invested for many years together before founding BTV and wrote checks into Mercury, Flexport, Ramp, and Hippo Insurance to name a few.
context.claim: The profile reports that Mohnot and Jake invested together before founding BTV and wrote checks into Mercury, Flexport, Ramp, and Hippo Insurance.

context.quote: As for Sheel, before BTV he ran 500 Fintech for close to 7 years, and before that was a founder, founding two companies, both of which were acquired.
context.claim: The profile reports that Mohnot ran 500 Fintech for nearly seven years after founding two companies that were acquired.

context.quote: 20VC Aug 14, 2022 Posted by

context.quote: Prior to founding BTV, Sheel honed his expertise through various ventures, including co-founding FeeFighters, a payments startup acquired by Groupon in 2012, and Innovative Auctions, which was sold in 2015.
context.claim: The profile reports that Mohnot co-founded FeeFighters, acquired by Groupon in 2012, and Innovative Auctions, sold in 2015.

context.claim: The episode describes Mohnot's firm BTV as an early-stage fintech investor that leads pre-seed and seed rounds.

context.quote: He also invested in numerous tech companies as an angel investor, successfully achieving two meaningful exits in fintech companies.

context.quote: In this episode, Sheel Manot, founder of Better Tomorrow Ventures (BTV), and his wife, Amruta Godbole, discuss the intricacies of fundraising, both for startups and venture capital funds.
context.claim: The episode description, which misspells Mohnot's surname, presents him as a Better Tomorrow Ventures founder discussing startup and fund fundraising.

context.quote: Sheel emphasizes the importance of persistence, grit, and speed in navigating the challenging landscape of fundraising, sharing his personal experience of funding 500 Fintech from his own pocket before securing external capital.
context.claim: The episode description reports that Mohnot emphasizes persistence, grit, and speed in fundraising and initially financed 500 Fintech personally.

context.quote: With FinTech falling in and out of favor, BTV has adapted by investing in companies targeting broader markets, such as banks and e-commerce.
